instruction.name: x86rcri.w
instruction.description: x86-style rotate right through carry by immediate on 32-bit values.

experiments.name: flags read-write loop
experiments.init: li.d $r12, 5; li.d $r13, 7; li.d $r4, 9; li.d $r5, 11; li.d $r6, 13; li.d $r7, 15; x86mtflag $r12, 0x3f; armmtflag $r12, 0x39
experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 20000 --unroll2 40000 --iters 100 --warmup 10 --reps 10 --init 'li.d $r12, 5; li.d $r13, 7; li.d $r4, 9; li.d $r5, 11; li.d $r6, 13; li.d $r7, 15; x86mtflag $r12, 0x3f; armmtflag $r12, 0x39' --asm 'x86rcri.w $r12, 1'

latencies.notes: EFLAGS -> EFLAGS: the instruction reads and writes the flag register, so one copy already forms a chain and the measured 2.00 cycles are the read-modify-write path. An earlier chain appended `x86mtflag rd, mask`, but these instructions write no GPR, so that pair had no dependency and only reported the length of a dependency-free sequence.

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.notes: rd -> EFLAGS chain closed by x86mfflag; 1 cycle is subtracted.

latencies.notes: rd -> EFLAGS chain closed by x86mfflag; 1 cycle is subtracted.

notes: LBT x86-style instruction with an immediate operand. Latency is recorded for the rd accumulator path and the EFLAGS path. Only EFLAGS is written: the general-purpose registers are read-only sources for this instruction (verified with a native test program, where every GPR keeps its value after execution while EFLAGS changes as documented, e.g. x86sub.b of 6 and 7 sets CF, SF, PF and AF). Throughput is not measurable for this instruction: it reads and writes the architectural flag register, so every copy depends on the flags written by the previous one and a body of copies is a dependency chain, not a set of independent lanes. Eight copies take 16 cycles, which is exactly the 2-cycle read-modify-write latency, so the only number that can be quoted is that a stream of flag-modifying instructions runs at one per two cycles. The `throughput` array is therefore empty; see the latency entry from EFLAGS to EFLAGS.
